scope: Proposition D.7 (Relative lifting) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 122-123. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Fix s ≥ 1, put k = s + 2, and fix a sufficiently large dimension n0 = n0(s) and ε0 > 0. There is an exponent E, depending only on these fixed parameters, with the following property. Fix the side-comparability constant R = 2n0+1. Let p ≥ 2, e−p ≤ a ≤ Λ ≤ 1, and suppose an absolute rule holds on every sufficiently large prime-sided box of dimension n0, with distinct sides and largest side at most R times the smallest: every progression-free input of mean at least a has, on a parameter slice of cost at most p, a degree-s patch of rank at most d0, complexity at most p, and score at least e−p against input minus Λ. The cutoff on every prime side is at most ep. Let Q be any box of dimension between 1 and p, with all sides at least exp((2 + p)E). Suppose 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 is progression-free on Q, and an old degree-s patch B of rank d and complexity at most p satisfies EQ(f − a)B ≥ e−p . Then some parameter slice of Q, of cost at most (2 + p)E, carries a degree-s patch B′ satisfying rank B′ ≤ d + d0, complexity(B′ ) ≤ (2 + p)E , E f − (1 − ε0)Λ  B′ ≥ exp(−(2 + p)E ). 122 There is also a separate impossibility alternative: if e−p ≤ a ≤ 1 and the absolute rule states that no such input of mean at least a exists, the old positive score is impossible. This alternative has no target parameter Λ. The exponent is independent of the absolute rule, of d, d0, and of every variable dimension included in p.
